target_customer: Software product and support teams that want in-app onboarding and guidance without building manual product tours
problem: Users cannot find features and tours break when the UI changes. Layup offered an AI second cursor inside the product that guides users in real time.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for in-app guidance
product_category: Digital adoption platform, AI in-app guidance

founders.name: Ryan Xue
founders.background_notes: YC page: first business hire at Origin, consultant at McKinsey, policy fellow at Google; later co-founded Andco (X26).

founders.name: Badal Jain
founders.background_notes: YC page: founding engineer at an early stage startup. Role conflicts between sources (CTO versus COO); the Whatfix announcement calls him co-founder and CTO.

founders.name: Michael Lemm
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and COO, later co-founder of Andco (X26).

exit.reason: Whatfix announced it welcomed the Layup team on 2025-11-25; the announcement describes team members joining rather than a purchase price or acquisition

competitors.traction_then: established vendor, no figures in the source

competitors.traction_then: established vendor, no figures in the source

competitors.traction_then: established vendor, no figures in the source

technical_complexity.rationale: A cursor agent that understands a live UI, adapts as the UI changes and respects roles and permissions needed browser level engineering and LLM grounding in early 2023.

defensibility.rationale: The launch post positions incumbents as outdated and fragile, but they could add LLM guidance, and other AI guidance startups were appearing; no data or network moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Whatfix announced it welcomed the Layup team on 2025-11-25, with the CTO leading engineering for Whatfix Seek and the CEO and COO advising on strategy.

market_need_then: The Layup launch post says help centers and rigid product tours leave users unable to find features and that incumbents are outdated, expensive and fragile; it gives no spend data.

branding.domain_note: Uses layuplabs.ai with the Labs suffix; several unrelated Layup companies exist.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and concise short lines such as Effortless guidance. Effortless growth.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable product metaphor in the tagline but the name collides with other Layup companies and no community or press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Layup built an AI second cursor for in-app onboarding against established adoption platforms and raised about $500K in 2023 per an aggregator. In November 2025 Whatfix, one of the incumbents it named, welcomed the team, with the CTO moving to engineering and the CEO and COO advising. The sources describe a team joining without a stated price, which fits a soft landing; the founders went on to start Andco in YC X26.
notes: The seed rests on VCBacked (Layup Labs, New York, April 2023, Leonis Capital); another VCBacked page for Mountain View names YC, Soma Capital and TSVC, and Whatfix says Layup was backed by YC, Soma and Leonis. CB Insights shows $9M and Employbl $2M seed, which probably belong to other Layup companies, so they are not recorded. The launch post for competitors states 'almost 2 years ago' without a date, so source_date is null; Pendo, WalkMe and Whatfix existed years before the batch. The Whatfix page shows a joining banner dated April 7, 2026 per a fetch summary, while the Whatfix announcement is dated November 25, 2025 in a search summary.
